headline: Hot NFP (165K vs 65K) and a dollar/yields rip collide with an NQ +1.4% bounce into the overnight highs after Thursday's −6% NDX rout. Lean SHORT at the open below the overnight high 27,251; flip LONG only on a reclaim and hold of 27,251.
session_note: Cash open 9:30 AM ET (10:30 AM Atlantic) · morning window · October NFP out 8:30 · Fed's Musalem 9:10, Bowman 12:15, Daly 1:00 PM ET · UMich 10:00 AM ET

flip.long: LONG if NQ reclaims and holds the overnight high 27,251.25 (≈ NDX ~27,129 on Thursday's ~122-pt premium), meaning the chip short-cover is overpowering the hawkish NFP. Target a push toward 27,400–27,500.
flip.short: SHORT stays on while NQ is below 27,251. Stronger below the overnight midpoint ~26,809 (≈ Thu settle 26,752 area); next targets Thursday's settle 26,752 then the overnight low 26,366.50.

thesis: A low-conviction lean **SHORT** for the open. **NQ is +379.25 pts / +1.42% at 27,131.25 (≈9:10 AM ET)** after Thursday's historic AI rout (NDX −6.36% to 26,629.81), sitting in the upper half of a 26,366.50–27,251.25 overnight range [1]. The bounce is real in chips — **AMD +8.2%, AVGO +5.5%, MU +6.1%, NVDA +4.0%** premarket — but megacaps are mixed-to-soft (MSFT −1.0%, AAPL −0.8%, META −0.4%) [2,3]. Macro cuts against extending it: **October NFP printed 165K vs 65K expected**, unemployment 4.1% vs 4.2%, AHE +0.4% m/m / +3.1% y/y, and Aug–Sep revised up a combined +84K [4,5]. **December hike odds jumped to ~76%** (CME FedWatch via CNBC), the 10-year is +3 bp near 4.87%, and the dollar is +0.7% at 102.27 [6,7]. Tape is split: Dow futures −0.9%, S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq +1.4% [2,3]. VIX is still elevated at 26.5 after Thursday's spike to 28.18 [7]. So **lean short below the overnight high 27,251; flip long only on a reclaim and hold**.
evidence_cutoff: Fri Nov 6, 2026, 9:10 AM ET (10:10 AM Atlantic). Futures and premarket stock quotes ~9:05–9:11 AM ET (Yahoo, may be delayed). NFP 8:30 AM ET print.

bullets.label: NFP was a full hawkish beat.
bullets.text: Payrolls 165K vs 65K, U-rate 4.1%, wages hot, and two-month revisions +84K [4,5]. December hike odds moved up to ~76% [6]. That is duration-negative for NQ into the open.

bullets.label: The bounce is already extended.
bullets.text: NQ is +1.42% at 27,131.25, in the upper half of 26,366.50–27,251.25 and only ~120 pts under the overnight high [1]. Chips are leading the cover (AMD +8%, NVDA +4%) after Thursday's −6% NDX wipeout [2,3].

bullets.label: Dollar and yields confirm the hawkish read.
bullets.text: DXY +0.7% at 102.27 and the 10-year +3 bp near 4.87% [7]. Futures showed little lasting equity reaction to the print itself, which often means the bounce fades into cash [2].

bullets.label: The tape underneath is still soft.
bullets.text: Dow futures −0.9% while Nasdaq +1.4% and S&P +0.2% — a chip-led bounce, not broad risk-on [2,3]. VIX is still 26.5 [7].

bullets.label: Bull case:
bullets.text: After NDX's worst day since March 2020 (−6.36%), short-covering can run into and through the cash open. Yardeni called the AI selloff a "buying opportunity," and Citi said data-center buildout may slow rather than stop [2]. VIX is off Thursday's 28.18 high, and chips are bid hard premarket [3,7].

bullets.label: Bear case:
bullets.text: Hot NFP plus a stronger dollar and higher yields give the Fed cover to hike in December. Megacaps are not confirming the chip bounce, Dow futures are still red, and NQ is leaning into overnight supply at 27,251.

bullets.label: Flip to LONG:
bullets.text: NQ reclaims and holds the overnight high 27,251.25 in the first 30 minutes. Target 27,400–27,500.

bullets.label: Stronger SHORT:
bullets.text: NQ loses the overnight midpoint ~26,809 / Thursday settle 26,752. Next target the overnight low 26,366.50.

bullets.label: Go STAND ASIDE:
bullets.text: NQ chops between ~26,900 and 27,251 with chips and megacaps cancelling and VIX stuck mid-20s.

bullets.label: Wildcards:
bullets.text: Musalem (9:10), Bowman (12:15) and Daly (1:00 PM ET); UMich sentiment at 10:00 AM ET; more AI / data-center policy headlines after the midterm sweep; weekend positioning after a −6% NDX day [8].
